Air Force Falcons.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Troy Calhoun as the second-longest tenured coach in college football, entering his 20th season.
Air Force Falcons.dc: Steve Russ, most recently in the same role at UAB and previously Air Force's coordinator from 2014 to 2017.
Air Force Falcons.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Air Force Falcons.dc_status: New — the guide records Calhoun hiring Russ, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Air Force Falcons.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Air Force Falcons.offensive_scheme: Named as an option offense, and the guide draws a scheduling consequence from it: it wonders how conference newcomers, two of whom Air Force hosts, will cope with preparing for an option offense in the middle of the regular-season grind.
Air Force Falcons.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide states the contrast bluntly — the Falcons paired one of the nation's best offenses with quite literally its worst defense: 30.3 points and 423 yards allowed per game, 7.2 yards per play conceded, dead last nationally in opponent EPA per play, 134th in net yards per play at -2.08 and 96th in success rate.
Air Force Falcons.run_pass: Run-weighted by scheme. The guide records Air Force ranking 15th nationally in both rushing EPA per play and rushing success rate.
Air Force Falcons.qb_development: Not addressed as a record, but the guide records a rare circumstance: this is the first time in four years Calhoun has a returning quarterback, and it rates Liam Szarka the best quarterback Air Force has had in years.
Air Force Falcons.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 13.
Air Force Falcons.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive coordinator, and the replacement is a returnee to the programme — Russ held the same job at Air Force from 2014 to 2017.
Air Force Falcons.prior_school: UAB is Russ's most recent stop, and Air Force itself is his earlier one.
Air Force Falcons.vsin_assessment: Expectations low and the hinge named precisely. The guide frames a 4-8 season as inconsistent with expectations for the second-longest tenured coach in college football, then says Calhoun now has what he needs — an experienced quarterback, returning production from one of the country's most efficient offenses, and no expectations, with attention on UNLV, New Mexico and North Dakota State instead. On the defense its summary is that there is nowhere to go but up. Given Calhoun's consistency it sees a possible surprise appearance in the Mountain West Championship, something that has not happened since 2015.
Air Force Falcons.strengths: A 20-year head coach with an offense that ranked 11th nationally in EPA per play, the first returning quarterback in four years and the best the guide says Air Force has had in years, a strong offensive line, eight returning defensive starters including eight of the top nine tacklers, a coordinator who has done this job here before, and a scheme opponents must specially prepare for.
Air Force Falcons.concerns: The worst defense in the country by opponent EPA per play, only four returning offensive starters with three offensive line starters departed, and a new coordinator installing his ideas on that defense.
Air Force Falcons.betting: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, and the guide names the hinge precisely — the defense. Creeping back toward merely average would make Air Force a true Mountain West threat.

Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.dc: Dennis Thurman, back for a second year.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.dc_status: Returning — Thurman enters year two, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide traces the trajectory instead: from Timmy Chang's 2022 arrival, when Hawaii had two returning starters and allowed 34.7 points and 6.6 yards per play, every season since has allowed fewer points and yards per game, improved yards per play, and raised sacks from 17 in 2022 to 30 last season.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.qb_development: Addressed as a developmental question rather than a coaching record. The guide records Micah Alejado completing 66% for 3,106 yards with 24 touchdowns to nine interceptions through a nagging ankle injury, adds that the Las Vegas native was never a dual threat in high school yet showed he could escape pressure and use his legs after rushing for 614 yards and six touchdowns over his final two seasons at Bishop Gorman, and expects passing improvement given his pedigree.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 0 for 7 returning starters — totalling 14.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.vsin_assessment: Improvement as the stated theme, with a modest and explicit standard. The guide says improvement is the theme under Chang, who has bettered his record every season with statistical gains on both sides of the ball, and notes preseason all-conference selections at quarterback, receiver, linebacker and defensive back. Its defensive standard is deliberately modest: Hawaii does not need a shutdown unit, so maintaining or slightly improving on last season should make this a strength. It closes on the trend, suggesting the programme is on the brink of something big.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.strengths: A head coach who has improved his record every season, full staff and quarterback continuity, a preseason Offensive Player of the Year, four preseason all-conference selections, a second-year defensive coordinator with a four-year improvement trend behind him, and hosting all three teams ranked ahead of Hawaii in the market.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.concerns: Only seven returning starters with three back on defense, and a quarterback whose added running dimension depends on a healthy ankle.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.betting: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, hinging on Alejado's growth — and the guide notes he has given no reason to doubt it, with a plethora of weapons available. It records the market having Hawaii on the fringe of contention as the fourth choice at DraftKings at +450.

Nevada Wolf Pack.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.

Nevada Wolf Pack.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Nevada Wolf Pack.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split, though the guide links the phases: if the passing game returns to average it could do wonders for a run game showing strong forward indicators.
Nevada Wolf Pack.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide explains why a three-way competition exists despite Carter Jones returning, expects UCLA transfer Luke Duncan to win eventually while recording that Choate insists the race is tight going into camp, and concludes that whoever wins, Nevada needs far more from the position.
Nevada Wolf Pack.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 5 returning starters, totalling 7.
Nevada Wolf Pack.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator per the Stability Score table.
Nevada Wolf Pack.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Luke Duncan from UCLA, and Jacob Norcross and Ethan Newman Jr from Memphis.
Nevada Wolf Pack.portal_recruiting: Addressed at specific positions — a UCLA transfer at quarterback and two Memphis linemen at center and right guard.
Nevada Wolf Pack.vsin_assessment: Character credited, trend used as the argument. The guide rates Jeff Choate a fiery coach with a sturdy base that could produce improvement, says his defensive background means this unit's effectiveness will always be in question, and grounds its expectation in trend: Nevada has allowed fewer points, fewer yards per game and fewer yards per play in each year under Choate, and it would not be surprised to see that continue.
Nevada Wolf Pack.strengths: A three-year defensive improvement trend under a defensive-minded head coach, defensive-coordinator continuity, four preseason all-conference players across both lines and the secondary, three returning offensive line starters including a preseason all-conference left tackle, and two Memphis transfers added inside.
Nevada Wolf Pack.concerns: A 3-9 season, only five returning starters, a new offensive coordinator, an unsettled three-way quarterback competition, and a passing attack ranked 133rd in EPA per play.
Nevada Wolf Pack.betting: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, argued through the staff: the guide judges Luke Duncan showed enough in his Hawaii starts to expect he wins the job and performs admirably, sees enough offensive talent to be much more effective with a steadier hand, and assumes Choate gets the most from the defense.

New Mexico Lobos.vsin_assessment: A breakthrough acknowledged and a role-change problem identified. The guide records Jason Eck's Lobos taking the Mountain West by storm at 9-4 with six conference wins and being the conference favorite with one of the country's most experienced rosters. Its decisive reservation is situational: New Mexico closed as an underdog in seven games, but in the six where it was favored it went 3-3 straight up and just 1-5 against the spread — and this season the market will make it a favorite in most contests. Its closing thought is a general principle applied to this team: being the underdog makes a nice story, but meeting market expectations as the hunted is a different task.
New Mexico Lobos.strengths: A Stability Score of 16 with everything returning, 12 returning starters on one of the country's most experienced rosters, the reigning conference Defensive Player of the Year at linebacker, and a defense strong at limiting explosive plays.
New Mexico Lobos.concerns: A quarterback recovering from throwing-elbow surgery with a capable challenger behind him, a defensive line that lost considerable production, and a documented failure to perform as a favorite — 3-3 straight up and 1-5 against the spread in those spots.
New Mexico Lobos.betting: The guide's coaching-adjacent market argument is the favorite-role record: 3-3 straight up and 1-5 against the spread when favored, with the market set to make New Mexico a favorite in most contests. It also tells bettors to anticipate a dip from 36 sacks.

North Dakota State Bison.qb_development: Identified as a programme tradition being tested. The guide records Cole Payton going to the Eagles at pick 178 as the fifth Bison starting quarterback drafted in 11 years, notes Nathan Hayes has been in the system since 2022 so there should be no learning curve, and supplies the counterweight — he takes over an offense missing its top two rushers and top two receivers.
North Dakota State Bison.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 12.
North Dakota State Bison.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
North Dakota State Bison.portal_recruiting: The defining subject for this programme, and the guide treats it as a deliberate model under test. North Dakota State took a different approach from most, signing 29 high school players and only nine transfers, of whom three played at Power Four programmes last season — one being punter Caleb McGrath — while losing significant talent including two First-Team All-MVFC offensive linemen. The guide explains why the model worked before and why it may not now: recruiting and developing high school players succeeded at the FCS level, but Group of Five teams constantly retool with castoffs and former top prospects seeking a new home. With just 10 starters back and zero portal starters added, it leaves the question genuinely open.
North Dakota State Bison.vsin_assessment: A formula, not just a team, under examination. The guide identifies roster construction as the distinguishing factor — a largely homegrown roster and few transfers, with Tim Polasek having lost considerable talent to the portal — and frames the season as a true test of the programme's formula. Its reasoning is specific: portal losses were immense with little brought back, and while the Mountain West is no power conference, these are teams built with former Power Four players carrying real talent, so there should be doubts about walking in and dominating. Its summary is that the days of bullying a lesser conference are gone.
North Dakota State Bison.strengths: Full staff continuity, a quarterback who has been in the system since 2022, a programme record of five drafted starting quarterbacks in 11 years, and familiarity with the favorite's role — NDSU was favored in every game last season and closed as a 30-plus point favorite in six of 13.
North Dakota State Bison.concerns: A roster model the guide says is being tested for the first time at this level, immense portal losses including two First-Team All-MVFC offensive linemen with zero portal starters added, only 10 returning starters, the loss of the top two rushers and top two receivers, and a schedule with road trips to Air Force, UNLV, New Mexico and Hawaii the guide calls coin-flip spots.
North Dakota State Bison.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked conclusion is that NDSU is certainly capable of winning the league, but the road is much tougher.
